transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
My sleep is completely off—I either lie awake most of the night or crash at odd hours and still wake up exhausted. It's gotten really hard to function during the day because of it.
Do your sleep problems mainly mean you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at night, or do you tend to fall asleep at inappropriate times during the day even when you want to stay awake?

It's mostly that I lie awake for hours with my mind racing and can't fall asleep until 3 or 4 a.m., then I either wake up early feeling panicky or sleep past my alarms. I don't suddenly fall asleep during the day when I'm trying to stay awake, but I do end up crashing at odd times just because I'm so completely exhausted.
How long has this sleep problem been going on, and does it happen even when you have enough time and a comfortable place to sleep?

It’s been building up for about two years since my breakup, but it’s gotten much worse over the last several months. It happens in my own comfortable bed in my apartment, even when I have plenty of time set aside to sleep. My mind just won't stop racing when I lie down, or I'll wake up feeling completely panicky.

When you have a chance to sleep, do you usually have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at night, or do you also have sudden episodes where you fall asleep unintentionally during the day even when you are trying to stay awake?

Like I said, I don't have sudden, uncontrollable sleep attacks during the day. My main issue is at night, where I lie awake for hours with my mind racing and struggle to fall asleep, and then I only crash during the day because I am so physically exhausted.
Do you ever have sudden, uncontrollable episodes of falling asleep during the day even when you are trying hard to stay awake, or is the problem mainly that you cannot sleep at night?

No, I don't have sudden, uncontrollable sleep attacks during the day. The issue is definitely that I can't sleep at night because my mind is racing, and I usually can't fall asleep until 3 or 4 a.m. Any sleeping I do during the day is just because I'm completely exhausted from such poor sleep at night.
When you finally do sleep, do you feel rested afterward, or do you still wake up feeling unrefreshed even after a full night in bed?

I don't feel rested at all when I wake up. Even on the days when I manage to sleep late into the morning, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted, like I've been hit by a truck. Other times, I just jolt awake after only a few hours feeling wired and panicky.

Do you have a regular pattern of falling asleep and waking up very late, but then feel fairly alert once you are on that schedule, or is your sleep problem mainly trouble sleeping no matter what schedule you keep?

It's definitely a struggle no matter what schedule I keep. I lie awake for hours with my mind racing and don't fall asleep until 3 or 4 a.m., and even when I do sleep in late, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted rather than alert. It always feels like I've been hit by a truck.
Do you usually fall asleep and wake up at about the same very late times every day, or do your sleep and wake times vary a lot from day to day?

My sleep schedule is highly inconsistent and varies a lot from day to day. Some nights I'll lie awake with my mind racing until 3 or 4 a.m. and then jolt awake at 6 a.m. feeling wired and panicky, while other days I sleep right through my alarms until late morning. Either way, I always wake up feeling completely exhausted.
Do you usually sleep and wake at the same very late times every day, or do your sleep and wake times change a lot from day to day?

They definitely change a lot from day to day, and there's no set pattern at all. Some days I'm up at 6 a.m. after barely sleeping, and other days I can't get out of bed until almost noon. It is completely unpredictable and inconsistent.
Have you ever had a fairly regular pattern of going to sleep and waking up at the same very late times every day, or is it always unpredictable with no stable sleep schedule?

No, I've never had a regular late-night routine; it has always been highly unpredictable and unstable. I'll lie awake for hours with my mind racing, sometimes only falling asleep around 3 or 4 a.m., and then I either jolt awake at 6 a.m. feeling panicky or sleep right through my alarms. Either way, I am left completely exhausted.
When you do sleep, do you usually get enough total hours of sleep for your age, or are you sleeping too little most nights because you can’t fall asleep or stay asleep?

I am definitely not getting enough restful sleep most nights. I often lie awake with my mind racing until 3 or 4 a.m., and on many days I jolt awake at 6 a.m. feeling panicky, meaning I only get two or three hours of sleep. Even when I do sleep longer, it is so disrupted that I still wake up feeling completely exhausted.
Have you ever had a stable pattern of sleeping and waking at the same very late times every day for at least several weeks, with you feeling fairly alert once on that schedule?

No, I’ve never had a stable late schedule like that, and I definitely don't ever feel alert. My sleep is completely erratic and unpredictable, where I'm either lying awake for hours or crashing at odd times. Whenever I do wake up, I just feel exhausted, panicky, or like I've been hit by a truck.
Do you ever have a stable pattern of going to sleep and waking up at the same very late times each day for at least several weeks, or is your sleep always irregular with no consistent schedule?

My sleep is always completely irregular with absolutely no consistent schedule. Some nights I lie awake for hours and only sleep from about 3 or 4 a.m. until 6 a.m. before jolting awake panicky, while other nights I sleep right through my alarms until late morning. It has made it completely impossible to establish any kind of stable routine.
When you are able to sleep on your own schedule, do you feel fairly normal and alert during the day, or do you still feel exhausted and unrefreshed no matter what?
I still feel completely exhausted and unrefreshed no matter what. Even when I am able to sleep on my own schedule or sleep in late, I always wake up feeling like I've been hit by a truck.

Have you been sleeping too little most nights because you cannot fall asleep or stay asleep, or is the main issue that you sleep at the wrong times and feel alert once you are asleep on a shifted schedule?

It’s really a combination of both. I lie awake in bed for hours with my mind racing and don't fall asleep until 3 or 4 a.m., and then I either wake up too early around 6 a.m. feeling wired and panicky, or I sleep late into the morning and still wake up feeling completely exhausted and unrefreshed.

When you are unable to sleep, is it mainly because you feel unable to fall asleep even though you want to, or do you often feel a strong urge to sleep at the wrong times and then stay awake when you need to be alert?

It is actually a mix of both. I lie in bed for hours with my mind racing, unable to fall asleep until 3 or 4 a.m. despite desperately wanting to, but then I also end up crashing at odd hours and sleeping through my alarms. When I finally wake up, I still feel completely exhausted, as if I've been hit by a truck.

Have you ever had a stable pattern of falling asleep and waking up at the same very late times for several weeks, and then felt fairly alert once you were on that schedule? Or is it always irregular and unrefreshing no matter what schedule you keep?

It is always completely irregular and unrefreshing, no matter what schedule I try to keep. I never feel alert or rested, and even when I do sleep late, I still wake up feeling either wired and panicky or completely exhausted like I've been hit by a truck.

Have you ever had a stable pattern of falling asleep and waking up at the same very late times for several weeks, and then felt fairly alert once you were on that schedule? Or is it always irregular and unrefreshing no matter what schedule you keep?

It is always completely irregular and unrefreshing, and I have never had a stable schedule. I just lie awake for hours with my mind racing, finally falling asleep around 3 or 4 a.m., and then I either wake up early feeling wired and panicky or sleep late and still feel like I've been hit by a truck.

Have you ever had a stable pattern of falling asleep and waking up at the same very late times for several weeks, and then felt fairly alert once you were on that schedule? Or is it always irregular and unrefreshing no matter what schedule you keep?

No, I have never had a stable late-sleep schedule where I felt alert. My sleep is always irregular and completely unrefreshing, no matter what. I just lie awake for hours with my mind racing until 3 or 4 a.m., and then I either jolt awake early feeling panicky or sleep late and still feel like I've been hit by a truck.

Have you ever had a stable pattern of falling asleep and waking up at the same very late times for several weeks, and felt fairly alert once you were on that schedule? Or is your sleep always irregular and unrefreshing no matter what schedule you keep?

My sleep is always completely irregular and never refreshing. Even on the nights when I finally doze off around 3 or 4 a.m. and sleep through to late morning, I still wake up feeling like I've been hit by a truck, or I'll jolt awake early feeling wired and panicky. There is just no stable or restful pattern to it at all.

When you have trouble sleeping, do you also have episodes of feeling unusually energetic, needing much less sleep than usual, or having racing thoughts because your mood is elevated rather than anxious?

No, I never have times where I feel unusually energetic or feel like I need less sleep. My racing thoughts are always driven by intense anxiety, panic, and worry, and I always end up feeling completely exhausted and drained rather than energized.
When you have trouble sleeping, do you ever have periods of feeling unusually energetic or needing much less sleep than usual, or is it always anxiety and exhaustion without increased energy?

It is always anxiety and exhaustion; I never experience a high-energy state where I feel like I don't need sleep. When I lie awake with my mind racing and wake up early, I just feel wired and panicky rather than energized, or I sleep late and still feel completely exhausted.
Do you snore loudly, stop breathing in your sleep, wake up choking or gasping, or have restless legs or frequent leg jerks at night?

I don't think I snore loudly, gasp for air, or have restless legs at night. My sleep issues are really just about lying awake for hours with my mind racing, and then waking up feeling either panicky or completely exhausted.

Outside of sleep, do you spend most days feeling excessive worry or tension about many different things that you find hard to control? For example, do you also have muscle tension, restlessness, or trouble concentrating during the day?

I don't really experience general muscle tension or physical restlessness; in fact, I often feel the opposite—completely slowed down or even frozen. My worries aren't really about general everyday things either, but are more focused on specific fears about my ex, my parents, and constantly feeling like a burden to everyone.

Do you feel excessive worry or tension about many different everyday things most days, or are your worries mainly focused on a few specific issues like your ex, your parents, or feeling like a burden?

My worries are not about general everyday things, but are very specifically focused on my ex and my parents monitoring me through people at my company. I also constantly feel like a burden to others and replay my past mistakes, which makes me feel like a horrible person who ruins everything.
Have you also had a persistent low mood or loss of interest in things most days, along with changes in appetite, energy, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love like painting and seeing friends, and I constantly feel so guilty and worthless over minor mistakes that I sometimes wish I could just disappear. I also have to force myself to eat, which has made my clothes get loose, and my energy is so low that trying to do anything feels like I'm moving through molasses.
Have you had thoughts of hurting yourself or that you would be better off dead, or made any plans to end your life?

I've definitely had thoughts that everyone would be better off if I just disappeared, especially when I'm replaying my mistakes and feeling like a horrible person. I don't have any active plans to end my life, but that heavy feeling of wanting to just fade away is very real for me.
Have you had any experiences like hearing voices, seeing things others don’t, or believing things that others say are not true, such as being watched or monitored?

Yes, actually. A few times a week when I'm alone at night, I hear a male voice telling me I'm a burden or being watched, which makes me get up and check every room. I also keep thinking my ex and parents have some kind of informal network at my company to monitor my movements and who I talk to, even though I logically know it sounds paranoid.
Do these experiences ever feel completely real to you, or do you usually recognize that the voice and the feeling of being watched might be part of your depression and not actually true?

In the moment, they feel incredibly real and frightening, even though a part of my brain logically knows it sounds paranoid and that no one is actually in my apartment. I still feel compelled to get up and check every room when I hear that voice, and I really struggle to shake the feeling that my ex and parents are somehow monitoring me at work.
Do you feel completely convinced that the voice and the belief that you are being watched are true, or do you recognize at least some of the time that they may not be real?

When it's happening, it feels completely real and terrifying, and I feel forced to get up and check every room. But during calmer moments, I have some logical insight and realize it sounds paranoid, that no one is actually in the house, and there is no real proof that anyone is monitoring me at work.
